target.name: seasonal_malaria_positivity_anomaly
target.baseline: expanding historical same-calendar-month median, years strictly before evaluation month

testing_bias.note: testing_down means positivity rose while tests fell >=15% and confirmed did not rise vs last year's same month.

statistical_convention_alert.rule: robust_z >= 2.0 AND n_prior >= 3 AND completeness >= 0.20 AND tests > 0

mild_convention.rule: robust_z >= 1.5 with the same eligibility gates

backtest.evaluation: chronological; baseline at t uses only earlier years of the same district-calendar-month

candidate_dual_gate_z2_and_abs_dev_ge_0..reason: robust_z>=2 alone fires on sub-1pp moves when MAD is near zero

baseline_comparison_predict_positivity_t.note: Persistence copies positivity(t). Seasonal median and prior-year use the past-only baseline of month t+1's own calendar month. The anomaly rule is a detector of unusual t, not a t+1 point forecast.

predictive_value.question: Does an unusual month t provide information about elevated malaria after t?

options.B: ANOMALY TARGET IS PROMISING AND ML MODEL IS JUSTIFIED
options.D: ANOMALY APPROACH IS NOT CURRENTLY DEFENSIBLE

recommendation.reason: Past-only expanding seasonal median is a defensible contemporaneous baseline. Robust z with n_prior=3 is MAD-fragile and needs a magnitude gate. Persistence still dominates t+1 positivity, so an ML forecast is not justified.
